verdict.rationale: First-party docs say a natural-language description produces a working app with frontend, backend, database, auth and integrations, backed by editable code and a built-in hosted backend that can be published in a few clicks (lovable-docs-1, -27, -32, -5, -28, -19). Hands-on community reports back this up: a startup CTO built internal CRUD tools and dashboards with it, and other users report solid scaffolding and prototypes (lovable-comm-9, -10, -5). Those same reports note mediocre code quality, everything packed into one JS file, trouble with complex integrations, and poor performance in one build (lovable-comm-1). Missing for 10: independent evidence that generated full-stack apps hold up beyond prototypes and simple CRUD tools, and maintainable code structure on more complex apps.
